summary: Deployed a sandboxed systemd service `inventory-worker` on node1 that runs a long-lived loop writing heartbeat lines every 5s into /var/lib/inventory/inventory.log. Confinement uses DynamicUser + StateDirectory=inventory + ProtectSystem=strict + ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory + NoNewPrivileges=yes plus a broad set of additional systemd sandbox hardening options. Verified writes outside the allowed path fail (read-only filesystem) and privilege escalation (sudo) is blocked by NoNewPrivs. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-reboot boot_id and healthy service state, rebooted node1 natively, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and confirmed the service auto-started (enabled) with a new PID and resumed writing to the same data file.
actions_performed: Wrote /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh (infinite loop writing timestamped heartbeat lines every 5s)

Wrote /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service with DynamicUser, StateDirectory=inventory, NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, and additional hardening (PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectKernel*, RestrictNamespaces, MemoryDenyWriteExecute, empty CapabilityBoundingSet/AmbientCapabilities)
Verified service active/enabled, confined writes landing in /var/lib/inventory/inventory.log, NoNewPrivs=1 in /proc/<pid>/status
Ran negative-control transient unit with identical sandbox props attempting to write to /etc -> failed with 'Read-only file system'
Ran positive-control transient unit writing to /var/lib/inventory -> succeeded
Ran privilege-escalation negative control (sudo under NoNewPrivileges) -> blocked by kernel no_new_privs
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service health, issued native reboot via nohup'd reboot command so ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Captured post-restart boot_id (changed) and confirmed service auto-started (enabled, new MainPID) and resumed writing to inventory.log

evidence.requirement: inventory-worker deployed as a managed (systemd) long-running background service
evidence.summary: systemctl status shows inventory-worker.service active/running with ExecStart, enabled at boot, PID and child sleep process visible

evidence.requirement: Service confined to write only inside /var/lib/inventory
evidence.summary: systemctl show confirms ProtectSystem=strict + ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory + DynamicUser=yes; log file grows inside that path; identical-sandbox negative control writing to /etc fails with 'Read-only file system' while positive control writing to /var/lib/inventory succeeds
systemctl show reports NoNewPrivileges=yes; /proc/<pid>/status shows NoNewPrivs:1; identical-sandbox sudo escalation attempt is rejected with 'no new privileges flag is set'
Captured boot_id 646e5f74-dc0e-45e7-9746-226c4351af28 plus active/enabled service state and fresh log tail before reboot
Backgrounded native reboot command returned 'reboot-acknowledged' immediately, followed by connection timeouts on subsequent probes confirming the node actually went down

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed after restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id is 9f497dce-abb9-473e-ba48-ae47143d1cd5, differing from the pre-restart value, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart service and data recovery on node1
evidence.summary: Service is active/enabled with a new MainPID (756) after reboot and inventory.log shows continuous new heartbeat entries with sandbox properties (NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths, DynamicUser) unchanged
